title: Al-Mutalammis and His Wife Umaymah
logline: A poet who fled a king comes home after years, on the very night his wife, believing him dead, is being married to another man; a verse answered by a verse reunites them, and the new groom steps aside with grace.
moral: Faithful love outlasts absence and rumour, and true generosity is knowing when to step aside.
tone: Tender and bittersweet with one long suspense (will he be recognised, will the groom fight?), a warm release and a light comic button. No villain on screen after the first 5 seconds.

beats.summary: The poet flees the king on a camel, by night.
Umaymah waits at the tent post, marking the years.
The rumour spreads: he is dead.
Under pressure she gives one reluctant nod.
On the wedding night he rises over the dune: alive.
The children tell him he is dead and his wife is marrying.
He enters covered; a guest stares, then looks away.
She sighs and begins a verse.
He answers in verse across the feast: I am near.
She knows his voice; the cloth comes down.
The groom rises: a held breath, then a smile.
He gives up his place and leaves without looking back.
The wedding night becomes the night of their reunion.

desertCamp (planned name, AN-044): a bedouin camp, world 1600 x 1230, ground y 900, built on skyCycle(u) + the desertRoad dune layers with road: false. Parts: (1) big black goat-hair tent with an open front, x 520..1080: three front poles at x 560, 800, 1040 (8 wide) from y 900 up to y 520, 470, 520; roof a sagging black band 40 thick with a red and white stripe along its lower edge, running pole top to pole top and down by guy ropes to pegs at x 440 and x 1160; inside back wall navy with blue dots; floor carpet red with yellow dots x 540..1060, y 895..930; two floorCushions 100 x 30 at x 740 and 860 (seat top y 870: person y 870 with sit 1, seat 'bench'). (2) small closed tent left, x 120..400, peak (260, 600), optional lit door slit. (3) three far tent silhouettes on the mid dune at x 1250, 1380, 1500 (60 wide), option farLit 0..1. (4) fire ring at x 1220: 6 stones in a 90-wide arc, 3 flame tongues up to 70 high, flame 0..1, flicker from K.noise(t). (5) palmTree at x 1420, h 430. (6) lamp string: rope from (560, 520) sagging to (800, 500), (1040, 520) and on to the palm at (1400, 500), with 7 hangingLamp at even spacing; option lamps = number lit (0..7) or an array of 0..1. (7) tally post = the front left pole (x 560); tallyMarks drawn at y 640..760. (8) front pass (layer 'front'): the three front poles and a dune lip across x 1250..1600 with its top at y 860, to rise from behind. Horizon gap for arrivals at about (1500, 840). Options: u, lamps, fire, farLit, deco 0..1 (small red, white and yellow flags on the rope between lamps), layer 'back' / 'front'. Returns anchors {ground, tent {x0, x1, poles, ridge}, cushions [{x, sitY}], post {x, top}, lamps [{x, y}], fire {x, y}, lip, palm}.

props.description: scroll (planned name): the poet's verse. Rolled: 46 x 14 paper tube with yellow end caps. Open: 70 x 46 paper sheet with 3 wavy lines and a tiny camel doodle (12 px) in the corner; fields open 0..1, rot. Carried in a hand (P.hands) or tucked in the sash (only the end shows).

verseRibbon (planned name, AN-103): spoken poetry as a paper band 34 wide following a bezier from the speaker's mouth; squiggle lines of 'writing' appear along it with draw-on 0..1; the end can curl (one 30-radius loop) and it can fade from the tail. Three colours of edge: red (Umaymah), blue (the poet), yellow (the groom). No real words are written on it.
Seven hangingLamp(ctx, x, y, t, {lit}) on the camp rope; each with its own lit value and swing(); a yellow halftone disc r 60 on the carpet under each lit lamp.
Library drum at r 34, hole 0, as a hand drum held on the knee by each drummer; squash 8 % on each hit.

tallyMarks(ctx, x, y, n): n short scratched strokes (each 22 high, 6 apart, slightly irregular from K.rng seed) in groups of five with the fifth across, white on the dark pole. n = 6 then 7. Scene-drawn, tiny.

scenes.summary: Night flight. The poet gallops out of the king's city on his camel; the king points after him from the wall; the rider shrinks into the dunes and the sky wheels through days and nights.

Camel runs along the track at ground y 900, rider head near y 520. From 5.06 the camel is on the mid dune line (y about 800) going right and getting smaller; moon top right.

subtitles.ar: هرب الشاعر المتلمس من الملك النعمان بن المنذر،|وغاب عن أهله زمنًا طويلًا.|انتظرته زوجته أميمة بقلق، ولم يصلها منه خبر يطمئنها،|حتى شاع بين الناس أنه مات ولن يعود.
subtitles.en: The poet al-Mutalammis fled King al-Numan|and remained away for a long time.|His wife Umaymah waited anxiously|until people began to believe he was dead.

subtitles.ar: كانت أميمة تحب زوجها حبًا كبيرًا،|ولذلك رفضت أن تتزوج غيره.|لكن أهلها قالوا إن عليها أن تبدأ حياة جديدة،|وإن الانتظار لا فائدة منه بعدما انقطعت أخبار الرجل كل تلك السنوات.
subtitles.en: Umaymah loved him deeply|and refused to remarry.|Her relatives urged her to begin anew,|arguing that years without news made further waiting hopeless.

subtitles.ar: كثر الذين طلبوا يدها،|واستمر ضغط أهلها عليها حتى وافقت أخيرًا، وهي غير مطمئنة إلى قرارها.|حددوا ليلة للزفاف، واجتمع الناس في الحي،|وسمعت أصوات الغناء والدفوف من الخيام.
subtitles.en: Many suitors came.|Finally she agreed reluctantly,|and the family arranged a wedding.|Songs and drums sounded through the camp on the appointed night.

subtitles.ar: وفي تلك الليلة نفسها عاد المتلمس من سفره،|ورأى الزينة وسمع الفرح.|سأل صبيانًا عن سبب الاحتفال،|فأخبروه أن أميمة، زوجة المتلمس الذي يظنونه ميتًا، تتزوج رجلًا آخر.
subtitles.en: On that very night al-Mutalammis returned|and saw the celebration.|Children told him that Umaymah,|the wife of the man everyone thought dead, was marrying someone else.

subtitles.ar: دهش الشاعر وتألم، ثم دخل بين الحاضرين دون أن يعرفه أحد.|رأى أميمة قرب العريس الجديد، وكانت حزينة رغم الاحتفال.|وعندما اقترب العريس منها، تنهدت وأخذت تردد بيتًا من الشعر.
subtitles.en: Shocked and hurt, the poet entered unnoticed among the guests.|He saw Umaymah grieving beside her new groom,|and she began to recite a sorrowful verse.

subtitles.ar: تساءلت أميمة في بيتها أين أصبح زوجها الغائب،|وفي أي أرض بعيدة يعيش إن كان حيًا.|لم يستطع المتلمس أن يصمت، فأجابها ببيت من شعره|يقول إنه قريب، وإنه لم ينس حبها.
subtitles.en: Umaymah wondered aloud in verse|where her absent husband might be.|Al-Mutalammis answered with his own verse:|he was close at hand and had never forgotten her.

subtitles.ar: عرفت أميمة صوت زوجها،|وفهم العريس الجديد حقيقة ما حدث.|لم يغضب الرجل ولم يخاصمهما، بل أنشد كلمات تدل على أنه سيتنحى،|ثم ترك لهما المكان وانصرف دون أن يعود.
subtitles.en: Umaymah recognized her husband’s voice.|The new groom understood at once|and, without quarreling, spoke graciously|and withdrew, leaving the reunited couple alone.

subtitles.ar: عاد المتلمس إلى أميمة بعد غياب ظنه الناس نهاية حياته.|وبقي الزوجان معًا في راحة وسرور بعد أن زال سوء الفهم،|وصارت ليلة الزفاف التي بدت حزينة يومًا لعودتهما إلى بعضهما.
subtitles.en: After an absence everyone mistook for death,|al-Mutalammis and Umaymah were together again.|The wedding night became the night of their reunion.

new_assets.name: desertCamp
new_assets.description: Bedouin camp, 1600 wide: open big tent with three poles and a carpet, small tent, far tents, fire, palm, lamp string, front dune lip; day, dusk and night by skyCycle. Reuses the planned name from AN-044 (same drawing with options; this film adds the lamp string, deco flags and the tally post). Full dimensions in sets.camp.
new_assets.implementation: New function desertCamp(ctx, o) in the story (later Library/sets/towns.js) following the towns.js pattern: bake the static back layer per option set (skyCycle is live, so bake dunes + tents without sky, or bake per u step), draw lamps and fire live with o.t, and a second call with layer: 'front' for the poles and the dune lip. Dunes: call desertRoad with road: false and sky: false, or copy its three dune polygons. Tent roof: one filled quadratic-curve band (K brush outline) in C.black with dot shading in blue; stripe trim as alternating red and white rects clipped to the band's lower edge. Return the anchors object.

new_assets.name: verseRibbon
new_assets.description: Poetry made visible (planned in AN-103): a paper band that unrolls from the speaker along a curve with squiggle writing, can curl at the end and feed a thought cloud.
new_assets.implementation: verseRibbon(ctx, pts, t, {p, w: 34, col, curl, fade, seed}): sample a cubic bezier through pts into about 40 points; draw the band as a polygon offset +-w/2 along the normals up to arc fraction p (paper fill, black brush edge, coloured thin inner line); writing = for each of 2 rows a polyline of small seeded zigzags (K.rng) clipped to the band; curl = continue the path as a spiral of radius 30 for the last 8 % ; fade = alpha ramp from the tail. Pure function of t through p.

new_assets.name: person faceCover
new_assets.description: Planned opt-in field faceCover 0..1 (AN-075, AN-087): a flap of the head cloth drawn across the lower face from the far side, hiding mouth and nose at 1 while the eyes stay visible; puff bulges it 3 px with breath or speech.
new_assets.implementation: In the person head draw (cast/people.js), after the face and before the headwear outline: a quadrilateral in the headwear colour (pal.hc, with hd dots) from the far cheek across to the near jaw, its top edge at eye-bottom height, slid in by faceCover; add 2 fold lines. Here the eyes must stay uncovered (the acting from 88.5 to 131.5 is eyes only). Default 0 keeps the regression identical.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: Planned wordless picture balloon (single and strip mode). Icons needed here: portraitMedallion (planned: a person's head in a yellow-rimmed circle r 40) of the poet, Umaymah and the groom; a plain X that can be drawn on, crack and fall; a ring; a tent with a sun; a horse silhouette with a strike line.
new_assets.implementation: iconBalloon(ctx, x, y, w, h, t, {p, tail, frames: [fn], strip}) using the style's box/balloon primitive for the outline; each frame callback draws in a 100 x 100 cell. portraitMedallion(ctx, x, y, r, personP): clip a circle, call person() scaled so the head fills it, then the yellow rim. The X is two brush strokes with draw-on; falling uses fallY and rot.

new_assets.name: musicNotes
new_assets.description: Planned: quaver glyphs rising from a point on seeded S-paths, rocking and fading (the song at 61.8, the notes that reach the poet at 72.1, the restart at 162).
new_assets.implementation: musicNotes(ctx, x, y, t, {t0, n, seed, col, to}): for i < n a note born at t0 + i * 0.25 follows x + sin path, y - 90 * age; glyph = filled ellipse 14 x 10 rotated -0.3, stem 30, flag curve; alpha by age; optional target point 'to' bends the path.

new_assets.name: scroll + tallyMarks
new_assets.description: The two small story objects: the poet's verse scroll (planned scroll with an open state and a camel doodle) and the tally of years scratched on the tent post.
new_assets.implementation: scroll: rounded rects and three sine polylines; open state scales the sheet height by open; the doodle is 5 strokes. tallyMarks: n seeded strokes with ctx.lineCap round, every fifth diagonal across the previous four.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English is a shortened translation in several paragraphs (P1 omits 'no news reached her to reassure her' and 'would not return'; P3 omits 'her family kept pressing' and 'the people gathered'; P7 omits 'left without returning'; P8 omits 'the couple stayed together in comfort and joy after the misunderstanding cleared'); both are kept verbatim as supplied.
SCRIPT: in P6 the Arabic 'في بيتها' is staged as 'in her verse' (as the English says), not 'in her house'; default: label HER VERSE and the recital stays at the wedding.
The poet covers his face with his head cloth to enter unrecognised (the script only says nobody knew him); default: keep the face cover from 88.5 to 131.5.
The rumour of his death is shown as his portrait under a plain X in a picture balloon, with no grave or body; default: keep it this soft.

Added small inventions to carry the story without words: a tally of 7 years on the tent post (the script says 'all those years', no number), a verse scroll keepsake, a passing horseman who brings no news, a flower the groom hands to the poet; default: keep all four, counter reads 7 YEARS.
The verses are shown as ribbons of squiggle writing, with no invented lines of poetry on screen; default: no readable verse text.
English comic lettering added (NEWS?, DEAD?, NO!, HE IS ALIVE!, WHERE?, RIGHT HERE!, THAT VOICE!, NO ANGER, THE PLACE IS YOURS, DUM! TAK!); default: keep, about 20 items including labels.
The setting is a bedouin tent camp (the script says 'the tents') and the poet travels by camel; default: desert camp, not a town house.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; scenes S2-S16 all use one world (desertCamp 1600 x 1230) with a keyed camera, so characters keep continuous positions: Umaymah's cushion x 860, groom's x 740, tally post x 560, drummers x 330 / 430, guests x 1150 / 1240, fire x 1220, the poet's entry from the right edge and the groom's exit to the left edge.

Word cues: build CUE from timing.json with w(p, n); every action's cue word and time are in creative_plan.json. Narration has no pauses of 0.6 s or more, and the word timings show only two real gaps (46.36-46.90 and 121.16-121.47), so only 4 quiet effects are listed: a pop at 46.63 (suitors), a chime at 121.3 (the breath before his answer), and a chime at 171.75 plus one soft drum thud at 172.6 after the last word. Do not add more; the picture carries the rhythm (drum hands, lamp pulses).
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for auto-blinks; give explicit lids where the plan names them (the held shock at 85.9, the freeze at 127.5) and use P.noBlink there.

Eyes-only acting from 88.5 to 131.5 (face covered): use lookAt / gazePlan, lid, brow and head drop; make the eye whites read at phone size (he is at least 240 px tall on screen in his key shots S9 and S12).
Seated wedding pair: person({y: cushion.sitY, sit: 1, seat: 'bench'}) on scene-drawn cushions; floor guests use seat: 'floor'. Standing up is the sit blend back to 0 with anticipate() and settleTo().

Drum beat: one onset grid of 0.4 s from 62.52 to 107.3 (hands stop by 108.2) and again from 163.3 to the end; drive both drummers (drummerB half a beat late), the groom's clapping, head bobs and the lamp-disc pulse from the same list (countedBeats). No drum sound effects on the grid: the narration is continuous.

Night look: skyCycle u 0.72 for S6-S16 with dayCycle(u).night to tint the dunes and tents; keep faces at full paper white inside the lamp discs so expressions stay legible. S2-S5 run at u 0.25 (S2), 0.2 (S3), 0.08 to 0.2 (S4), 0.3 (S5).
The heart is the Library heart prop (catalogue props 'fig, worm, heart'); use it exactly three times (24.66, 128.56, 168.78).
Camera: clamp as in the template; world is 1600 wide in the camp, so clamp x to [500 / z, 1600 - 500 / z]. Use twoShot() for S10, S13, S15. Apply shake nowhere: this film has no impacts.
The LATER card at 9.1 hides the cut from the road set to the camp set (camera key pair at the card's covered midpoint).
Subtitles: chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt from the subtitles array (| marks); Arabic in Noto Naskh Arabic 700, English in blue Bangers below.
warnings: desertCamp is a large new set (effort L) and almost the whole film plays on it; build and still-check it first.
The narration never pauses for 0.6 s; only 4 effects are planned (two inside the narration, two after it). If either inner one touches a word in the real audio, drop it rather than move it.

The person figure is front-facing only: 'looking back', 'turning away' and walking off are done with gaze, head offset, tip and travel direction, not a profile. The groom's exit wave with his back turned must be read from the arm and the travel, since a back view does not exist.
faceCover must leave both eyes clear; if the planned Library field hides the eyes at 1, cap it at about 0.7 here.
Three verse ribbons plus thought cloud in S11-S12 can crowd the frame: keep her cloud in the upper right, his ribbon at head height, and remove the cloud by 126.5.
Twelve seated or standing people appear in the wedding wide; keep guests to four plus two drummers and two children, each with a different delay, so nothing moves in unison.
